title: Cameras Roll in Venice for the Sequel to 'Upgraded'
summary:
Shooting is underway in Venice for "Upgraded 2," the sequel to Amazon MGM Studios' 2024 romantic comedy "Upgraded." Camila Mendes is returning as Ana Santos, and Leslie Bibb is set to star alongside her. So far, there are no indications of what Bibb's role is.

In the first film, Ana is an intern at a New York City auction house. She pretends to hold a higher job after she is upgraded to first class on her flight to London. During the flight, she impresses a wealthy young Englishman named William, played by Archie Renaux, who is connected to the high-society art world. The sequel is described as a modern-day "Cinderella" tale.

Cameras started rolling in Venice on October 21. In the sequel, Ana is now seemingly seeking to make her mark at the Venice Biennale art exhibition, described as the world's oldest contemporary art fair. Becca Gleason is directing the sequel, taking over from "Upgraded" director Carlson Young. Luke Roberts and Justin Matthews, who wrote the first film, also wrote the screenplay for the sequel.

Venice itself is part of the story. Gleason has been shooting on the terrace of Ca' Giustinian, the Biennale headquarters that overlooks the lagoon's Grand Canal. Filming has also taken place in the neo-Gothic Palazzo Franchetti near the Accademia bridge, which serves as a Biennale exhibition space, and at the Moro Venice restaurant.

The film will have a decidedly Italian flavor beyond Venice and the Biennale. After 12 days of shooting on the lagoon, principal photography will move to Rome, where 33 more days of shooting are planned, according to Italy for Movies. The production designer is Italy's Luca Tranchino, and the Italian company serving as executive producer on the sequel is Colorado Film.
why_it_matters: Filming on location shows how a real city and its art world can shape a story, and sequels let audiences follow characters they already know into a new setting.
